about.title: Seal Beach Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Seal Beach sees a steady stream of traffic where the 405 meets local streets like Seal Beach Boulevard and Route 1, and public records show 88 injury collisions and 123 injured people in the most recent year on file, with three lives lost. Weekends draw extra traffic near the pier and shopping areas, and collision reports show Saturday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. as a common time for crashes to happen. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the aftermath can feel overwhelming — medical visits, insurance calls, missed work. LawProactive isn't a law firm, but we connect injured Seal Beach residents and visitors with independent personal injury attorneys who work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Our service costs you nothing, and there's no obligation to move forward. We simply help you find someone who can look at what happened and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Acting Quickly Matters in California

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or public bus — was involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your situation before it passes.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault just reduces the amount. This matters on multi-vehicle stretches like the 405 where fault can be disputed.

items.title: Be Careful What You Say to the Other Insurer
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, and anything you say can be used to minimize your claim later. It's usually wise to let an attorney handle those conversations and help preserve evidence like photos, witness contacts, and traffic camera footage before it disappears.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Seal Beach?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government vehicle or road condition was involved — such as a city-maintained intersection — that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes six months. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a critical filing window.

items.question: What if my accident happened on the 405 near Seal Beach and involved multiple vehicles?
items.answer: Multi-vehicle collisions on corridors like the 405 can involve disputes over who was at fault and by how much. Because California uses pure comparative fault, you can still pursue compensation even if you're found partially responsible. An attorney can help sort out liability using police reports, witness statements, and any available camera footage.

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company after a crash?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer without speaking to an attorney first. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to reduce your payout later. An independent attorney can communicate with insurers on your behalf so you don't have to navigate that alone.
